transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Alex Rivera (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood Solutions), Priya Kapoor (CTO, OrchardMesh), Evan Brooks (NetEng, OrchardMesh), Sofia Li (Security)

Summary: Initial private/VPC onboarding conversation focused on network design and compliance constraints. Action items captured at end.

[00:00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you all making time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Alex our systems engineer. How are we doing?
[00:00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi Jordan, thanks. Doing good. We wanted to make sure we cover our network constraints and the EU-only requirement first.
[00:00:20] Alex Rivera: Awesome. Quick agenda - confirm topology, peering approach (cross-account peering, Transit GW), private endpoints options, and any security/KMS asks. Then next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:30] Evan Brooks: Yeah, that's the meat of it. We run a split VPC model, and most of our production services live in a EU-west-1 primary region. We need to ensure Redwood's private dataplane doesn't egress outside EU.
[00:00:45] Jordan Park: Got it. So you're looking at Redwood Private deployment in a VPC-onramp model; that gives you the private control plane and the data path stays in your VPCs. Correct?
[00:00:55] Priya Kapoor: That's the intent. We evaluated hosted and dedicated — hosted is easier but compliance says data can't leave EU and we need customer-managed keys. Dedicated was better but still want full network control.
[00:01:10] Maya Singh: Quick note — our Private offering supports VPC peering, privatelinks, and also a transit-gateway connector for cross-account setups. We usually recommend privatelink for cross-account privacy but Transit GW makes sense at scale.
[00:01:24] Evan Brooks: Our infra team prefers Transit Gateway for central egress controls. We have a shared-services account that handles NAT and outbound proxies. How does Redwood's private endpoints integrate with a Transit GW?
[00:01:37] Alex Rivera: So, two main patterns we see: 1) Peer Redwood's service VPC into your Transit GW attachments (cross-account peering + route propagation), or 2) run privatelink endpoints into each consuming VPC. The former is easier when you have centralized routing; the latter minimizes cross-account route exposure. Both can respect region restrictions.
[00:01:56] Sofia Li: And what about allowlisting egress IPs? We need static IPs for external SaaS integrations. Does Redwood provide static egress IP ranges for Private?
[00:02:08] Jordan Park: For Private we can expose fixed egress IPs via a managed NAT box in your VPC or allowlist the Redwood egress ranges if you prefer our managed path. For Dedicated/hosted customers fixed IPs are possible via egress endpoints but for Private the customer-controlled NAT is common.
[00:02:26] Priya Kapoor: So you'd prefer we manage the NAT? We want ownership but also don't want to babysit the box.
[00:02:33] Maya Singh: Typically customers put in a small NAT fleet behind the Transit GW and that handles egress with SNAT. Redwood's runtime will respect the routing table. We'll provide guidance for sizing and HA.
[00:02:46] Evan Brooks: Ok. About DNS and split-horizon — we have internal names for our services. If we use privatelink, will we need to override public DNS or add conditional forwarding?
[00:02:59] Alex Rivera: Good question. For privatelink you usually get private hosted zone entries that you can associate with your VPC. For peering/transit setups you might need conditional forwarders to your internal resolver. We can share a DNS playbook — some customers point a Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint at Redwood.
[00:03:17] Priya Kapoor: Another constraint: HSM-backed keys. We use an external HSM provider and cannot export keys. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[00:03:26] Jordan Park: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS; we can accept CMEK patterns and some HSM integrations. We'll need details on your provider (vendor name, key wrapping model). That's an action item for security.
[00:03:40] Sofia Li: We run YubiHSM with an internal key wrap. Also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. How long are Redwood's audit logs kept on Private?
[00:03:49] Maya Singh: For Private deployments we can configure log retention; default is 90 days but enterprise options can be extended and forwarded to your S3 or SIEM. We'll produce an audit log schema.
[00:03:59] Evan Brooks: Perf question — latency. Our SLAs are sub-60ms p99 for token generation on short prompts. Is that realistic inside a VPC peered deployment?
[00:04:12] Alex Rivera: It depends on region and instance sizing. With co-located inference nodes in EU-west-1 and good network path via Transit GW the p99 can be in that ballpark for smaller context lengths. For larger context/long generations latency will increase. We can run an initial baseline with your sample payloads — we'll need a representative prompt set.
[00:04:33] Priya Kapoor: Cost tradeoffs — we were comparing Dedicated capacity vs Private. Private seems operationally heavier but gives the compliance we need. Anything else to watch for?
[00:04:44] Jordan Park: Right — Private shifts more of the network and key management onto you, but gives you full control. Dedicated is a middle ground where we reserve capacity for you but still manage the network egress unless you request private peering. Discussed many customers go Dedicated first for throughput guarantees, then migrate to Private for compliance.
[00:05:02] Sofia Li: What about model variants and fallbacks? If we need a fallback in another region due to capacity, how does Redwood handle region locking?
[00:05:13] Maya Singh: We can configure smart routing policies. For strict EU-only we'd set routing to prevent fallbacks to other regions; for soft constraints we can provide fallback with notifications. It's configurable per policy.
[00:05:25] Evan Brooks: For cross-account connectivity, any IAM role or STS assumptions needed for privatelink?
[00:05:31] Alex Rivera: Privatelink typically uses service consumers creating an endpoint in their account with an interface ENI. For peering/transit attachments we may need a small set of IAM permissions for the initial setup automation if you opt into our onboarding scripts, or you can apply them manually.
[00:05:47] Priya Kapoor: We prefer manual control. Another thing: data residency enforcement at storage layer — session KV caches, etc. Do you persist cache to our VPC?
[00:05:58] Jordan Park: For Private we co-locate KV caches inside your VPC — they do not leave the network. For hosted, caches are in Redwood-managed infra. We'll note the distinction in the whitepaper.
[00:06:10] Sofia Li: Sounds good. Can we get the security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence?
[00:06:16] Jordan Park: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC 2 type II report and our security pack. Note some redactions are standard.
[00:06:24] Evan Brooks: On the practical side, what data do you need from us for the network handoff?
[00:06:29] Maya Singh: Minimal list: VPC IDs, CIDR blocks (all accounts involved), Transit GW attachments or peering preferences, desired privatelink endpoints, intended egress IP strategy, and who owns the KMS/HSM. Also any IP allowlists for downstream services.
[00:06:45] Priya Kapoor: We'll compile that. Timeline-wise we want pilot in six weeks, full rollout in 3 months. Is that feasible?
[00:06:54] Alex Rivera: Six-week pilot is reasonable if we get the network details quickly and run a small inference baseline. Full rollout in 3 months depends on compliance gating and scale testing but is plausible.
[00:07:05] Jordan Park: Quick commercial note — pricing differs for Private (platform license + infra) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity). I'll follow up with a high-level cost comparison doc in the next email.
[00:07:16] Priya Kapoor: We'll need that for procurement. Also: any limitations with MFA, SSO? We use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning.
[00:07:25] Maya Singh: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning in Private and Dedicated. For some on-prem setups we need a connector but typically it's standard.
[00:07:34] Evan Brooks: A tiny nit — do you support static IP allowlisting for callback webhooks from the model responses?
[00:07:40] Alex Rivera: Yes — you can have webhook egress go through your NAT egress IPs in Private, so your downstream partners see your static IP.
[00:07:48] Priya Kapoor: Great. Anything else we should flag now?
[00:07:52] Sofia Li: One more security ask: can audit logs be forwarded in near real time to our SIEM rather than batch?
[00:07:59] Maya Singh: Yes, near real-time forwarding via Kinesis or direct syslog is possible — we'll include options in the security pack.
[00:08:08] Jordan Park: Alright let's capture next steps. We'll send the network checklist and SOC docs. Alex will prepare a benchmark plan. Priya/Evan will send CIDRs and transit diagrams. Sofia will send KMS/HSM details.
[00:08:20] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:08:23] Jordan Park: Thanks all — we'll follow up by email and book the technical deep dive for next week.

End of call notes / additional context:

- Not perfect transcript: some words may be mis-transcribed (eg. transit gw -> transit gateway, K-V cache -> KV cache).

Recap (at 00:08:20):
- Redwood to provide: checklist, security pack, cost comparison, perf benchmark plan.
